processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Heated up to 1250 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s
Held for 180 s to homogenize the austenite phase
Cooled to the corresponding deformation temperature at a rate of 10 °C/s
Kept for 60 s to reduce the temperature fluctuations
First stage: deformed at constant temperature 950 °C and strain rate 0.1 s⁻¹ to fixed strain ε=0.4
Second stage: strain rate transiently decreased from 0.1 s⁻¹ to 0.01 s⁻¹, then specimen compressed to final strain 0.9
Quenched in water immediately to freeze the high-temperature microstructure morphology

structures.overall_structure: Incomplete recrystallization state at 0.4 strain (end of first stage at 950 °C, 0.1 s⁻¹); coarse banded grains typical of incomplete DRX; DRX fraction 38.9 % (experimental GOS) / 42.9 % (3D CA).

microstructure_list.region: side section (EBSD reconstructed prior austenite grains)

structures.overall_structure: Nearly full recrystallization after the strain-rate decrease from 0.1 to 0.01 s⁻¹; refined equiaxed grains; DRX fraction 95.2 % (experimental GOS) / 99.1 % (3D CA).

microstructure_list.region: side section (EBSD reconstructed prior austenite grains)

structures.overall_structure: Final microstructure at 0.9 strain after strain-rate decrease; near-complete recrystallization with slight coarsening relative to 0.5 strain; DRX fraction 97.7 % (experimental GOS) / 99.8 % (3D CA).

microstructure_list.region: side section (EBSD reconstructed prior austenite grains)

measurement_conditions.environment: hot compression in Gleeble 1500; tantalum foil (0.1 mm) between specimen ends and indenter
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: transient strain-rate decrease at ε=0.4; total strain 0.9; water quenched after deformation

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Experimental flow stress at 950 °C for 0.1→0.01 s⁻¹ (0.4 strain): first stage at 0.1 s⁻¹ holds the high stress level, then drops abruptly at ε≈0.4 after the strain-rate decrease to 0.01 s⁻¹, softening to a minimum near 70–75 MPa; the 3D CA simulation reproduces the transient stress drop more closely than Model 1 (Fig. 8d, Fig. 13b).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 950 °C; strain rate 0.1 s⁻¹ (stage I) → 0.01 s⁻¹ (stage II); ε₁=0.4; total strain 0.9; tantalum foil 0.1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: obtain flow stress-strain curves under transient strain-rate decrease
characterization_methods.key_findings: Flow stress drops abruptly at ε≈0.4 after strain-rate decrease and softens to ~70–75 MPa

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: side section ground with SiC papers, polished with 1 μm and 0.25 μm diamond pastes, etched with saturated picric acid solution
characterization_methods.purpose: observe prior austenite grains (PAGs) at the center of the side section

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SU5000 scanning electron microscopy (SEM) equipped with an EBSD detector
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished with 10 % perchlorate alcohol solution at 30 V and 0.25 A for 30 s; step size 0.65–1.3 μm
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize as-quenched martensitic microstructure and reconstruct prior austenite grains
characterization_methods.key_findings: For this sample: 0.4 strain AGS 81.50±6.32 μm; 0.5 strain AGS 52.92±3.35 μm; 0.9 strain AGS 50.71±3.29 μm

characterization_methods.purpose: calculate the equivalent diameter of each prior austenite grain (PAG) based on the corresponding area in metallography

characterization_methods.technique: prior austenite grain reconstruction from EBSD
characterization_methods.purpose: reconstruct PAGs from EBSD diagrams because the imparted strain may cause failure of standard etching for PAG size determination
distinguish recrystallized grains from deformed ones

computational_details.simulation_method: 3D cellular automaton (CA) with inhomogeneous dislocation density, dislocation density gradients and grain boundary sliding (GBS)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: RVE 550 μm × 550 μm × 550 μm; cell size L0 = 2.5 μm; initial dislocation density 10^11 m^-2; initial mixed-grain microstructure from reconstructed 2D section
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Simulated AGS and DRX fraction compared with EBSD reconstructed results for this sample: 0.4 strain 42.9%/82.68 μm, 0.5 strain 99.1%/50.78 μm, 0.9 strain 99.8%/52.58 μm (Fig. 20b); reproduces transient strain-rate-decrease microstructure evolution

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: constitutive model embedded in DEFORM 3D using Fortran language
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Model 2 load prediction tracks experimental force-stroke evolution better than Model 1 for the 0.1→0.01 s⁻¹ (0.4 strain) path (Fig. 10b)

computational_details.simulation_method: phenomenological constitutive model with modified t0.5 and stress softening coefficient ks (Model 2)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: stress softening coefficient ks applied when ε ≥ ε₁ (ε₁=0.4); saturation stress corrected under varying conditions
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Model 2 reproduces the post-step softening for 0.1→0.01 s⁻¹ (0.4 strain) more closely than Model 1 (Fig. 8d); overall varying-condition accuracy R²=0.9507, RMSE=3.0399 MPa, AARE=3.11 % (Table 3)

unmapped_findings: DRX fraction evolution (this sample, 0.1→0.01 s⁻¹ at 0.4 strain, 950 °C): experimental GOS 38.9 % at 0.4 strain (constant 0.1 s⁻¹ reference at transition), 95.2 % at 0.5 strain, 97.7 % at 0.9 strain; 3D CA 42.9 % at 0.4 strain, 99.1 % at 0.5 strain, 99.8 % at 0.9 strain (Fig. 20, blocks b0216/figure_020).

DRX fraction bar-chart values for decreasing strain rate at 0.4 strain (Fig. 18): Experiment 0.395 (0.4 strain), 0.955 (0.5 strain), 0.975 (0.9 strain); 3D CA 0.429, 0.991, 0.998 (block b0213/figure_018).

Simulated dislocation density distribution (Fig. 25) for transient strain-rate decrease 0.1→0.01 s⁻¹ at 0.4 strain: 0.4 strain ρ 1×10^11–3.689×10^14 m^-2; 0.42 strain ρ 1×10^11–1.133×10^14 m^-2; 0.45 strain ρ 1×10^11–7.167×10^13 m^-2; matrix grains A, B, C retain higher dislocation density than the constant 0.01 s⁻¹ case at 0.42 strain (ρ 1×10^11–5.169×10^13 m^-2, DRX 83.0 %) (blocks b0239/figure_025).

Table 7, row '950 °C, 0.1–0.01 s⁻¹ (0.4 strain)' at 0.9 strain: AGS of DRXGs_I = 46.11 μm, volume fraction of DRXGs_I = 0.24, AGS of DRXGs_II = 54.32 μm, volume fraction of DRXGs_II = 0.76, AGS of final microstructure = 52.58 μm (blocks b0250/table_007/b0251).

Final AGS after transiently decreasing Z_P is nearly unchanged relative to constant 950 °C/0.01 s⁻¹ (52.52 μm); remaining DRXGs_I volume fraction is low, so final grain size stays similar (blocks b0252/table_007).

Flow-stress behavior for this sample: first stage at 0.1 s⁻¹ holds high stress and drops abruptly at ε≈0.4 upon strain-rate decrease; experimental minimum near 70–75 MPa; Model 1 delays the predicted softening while Model 2 and the 3D CA reproduce the faster drop (Fig. 8d, Fig. 13b; blocks b0164/b0199).
